stories.title: Anthropic releases Claude Sonnet 5.5, faster and cheaper than Sonnet 5
stories.summary: Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 5.5, which it says runs over 30% faster and costs up to 30% less than Sonnet 5 while beating it on benchmarks, at the same price.
stories.more: Anthropic is positioning Sonnet 5.5 as a significantly cheaper, faster version of its mid-range model, cutting response times and token consumption. Simon Willison notes the model appears to beat Sonnet 5 on every benchmark he tried despite being priced the same. He also found Sonnet 5.5 shares a bug with Opus 5.5: at "max" thinking effort, it can burn through 128,000 tokens attempting his pelican-riding-a-bicycle SVG test and still fail to produce output.

stories.title: FuseReg regularizes layer fusion in representation autoencoders
stories.summary: A new method called FuseReg addresses the trade-off between fine pixel detail and generation quality when choosing which encoder layers to fuse in representation autoencoders.
stories.more: Representation autoencoders reuse a pretrained visual encoder's features as latents for both reconstruction and diffusion-based image generation. Choosing which encoder layers to fuse involves a trade-off, since shallower layers preserve pixel detail while deeper layers tend to improve generation metrics. Rather than relying on a fixed heuristic, the authors introduce FuseReg, a regularization approach to the layer-fusion choice that aims to close this reconstruction-generation gap.

However, RAEs still need to decide which encoder layers form the shared latent space for the generator and pixel decoder. This choice involves a trade-off. stories.title: Disaggregated Quantization splits LLM prefill and decode formats
stories.summary: A technique called Disaggregated Quantization (DQ) applies different precision formats to prefill versus decode phases of LLM inference, improving decode-heavy accuracy without added cost.
stories.more: Prefill and decode favor different quantization approaches: low-precision arithmetic speeds up prompt processing, while compact weights cut memory traffic during generation. The authors propose Disaggregated Quantization (DQ), which specializes compute formats, weights, and storage placement separately for each phase. Tested on Qwen 3 and Gemma 3, removing activation quantization specifically during decode improved accuracy on decode-heavy tasks without increasing inference cost.

stories.title: RayOrch orchestrates data pipelines for foundation-model training
stories.summary: RayOrch is a new system for programming and executing the large, uneven data-preparation pipelines used to build training data for foundation models.
stories.more: Preparing training data for foundation models requires pipelines that transform heterogeneous documents and videos into structured records, expanding each source item into a long-tailed, ordered sequence of children. GPUs need to batch these children across parents while preserving relationships, ordering, and completion status. The authors argue existing systems either hide parallelism behind coarse-grained jobs or expose too much complexity, motivating RayOrch as a lineage-controlled, multi-grain dataflow system for this problem.

items.excerpt: Preparing high quality training data for foundation models requires scalable pipelines that transform heterogeneous documents and videos into structured records. Such pipelines expand each parent item into an ordered and input dependent sequence of children, whose counts may be long tailed. stories.title: PISA brings log-linear complexity to block-sparse attention
stories.summary: A new block-selection method called PISA uses a pyramid top-K strategy to make block-sparse attention scale better for long-context language models.
stories.more: Scaling language models to long contexts is limited by the quadratic cost of self-attention, and block-sparse attention's usual bottleneck is that selecting which blocks to keep still requires scoring all query-block pairs, remaining quadratic in sequence length. The authors propose PISA, which gradually narrows candidate blocks using a pyramid top-K selection strategy instead of scoring everything at once, aiming to reduce this selection cost.

Block sparse attention offers an efficient alternative, but selecting the retained blocks remains a bottleneck. stories.title: InternW0-Δ unifies dynamics and action prediction for robots
stories.summary: InternW0-Δ is a World Action Model trained on over 20,000 hours of open data that combines visual dynamics prediction with action generation for generalist robots.
stories.more: World Action Models jointly model visual dynamics and action generation for generalist robot manipulation, but integrating priors like scene semantics, geometry, and motion from large pretrained models into one framework is a central challenge. InternW0-Δ is presented as a unified World Action Model pretrained on a heterogeneous corpus of over 20,000 hours of open data. The authors report it outperforms prior methods across both simulation benchmarks and real-robot platforms.

stories.title: Tactile-JEPA learns self-supervised representations for tactile sensors
stories.summary: Tactile-JEPA is a topology-aware self-supervised learning method aimed at distributed electronic-skin tactile sensors, an area largely unaddressed by prior vision-focused tactile encoders.
stories.more: Tactile sensing is important for contact-rich, dexterous robot manipulation, especially when vision is occluded, but unlike image encoders, tactile encoders are still typically trained from scratch on raw, noisy signals. Existing self-supervised approaches focus mostly on vision-based tactile sensors, leaving distributed electronic skins largely unaddressed. Tactile-JEPA is proposed as a topology-aware self-supervised representation-learning method targeting these distributed tactile sensors.

stories.title: Diffusion models refine satellite-derived digital surface models
stories.summary: Researchers use pretrained diffusion models conditioned on satellite imagery to clean up noisy digital surface models produced cheaply via stereo-photogrammetry.
stories.more: Large-scale digital surface models can be produced cheaply from satellite images via stereo-photogrammetry, but the resulting 3D maps often contain noise, outliers, and voids, whereas aerial LiDAR gives high accuracy at much higher cost. The authors study diffusion models conditioned on both photogrammetric surface models and Pléiades satellite imagery to refine vertically co-registered elevation maps, introducing a modified Stable Diffusion setup for this multimodal conditioning task.

The authors analyze 2,170 publicly available Jev projects collected from GitHub as of September 22, 2026, to understand usage patterns and how public attention relates to project distribution. They report rapid early growth in Jev's public ecosystem.

stories.title: FoMo proposes a new perceptual-distance metric for image generation
stories.summary: FoMo introduces the "forking moment" in a generative trajectory as a perceptual-distance measure for reference-based image quality assessment, aiming to reduce reliance on costly human scores.
stories.more: Reference-based image quality assessment metrics try to reflect how humans perceive the distance between a pair of images, and recent methods lean heavily on human-annotated data to model this. Mean-opinion-score pointwise scoring is easier to collect but is expensive at scale and often noisy due to inconsistent human judgments. FoMo proposes treating the forking moment in a generative trajectory as a perceptual distance metric instead.

items.title: FoMo: Forking Moment in Generative Trajectory as a Perceptual Distance
items.excerpt: Reference-based image quality assessment (IQA) metrics aim to reflect how humans perceive the perceptual distance between a pair of images. To learn how the human visual system (HVS) operates, recent reference-based IQA metrics heavily rely on human-annotated data. stories.title: TrackEverything tracks dense points over long videos via 3D scene tracks
stories.summary: TrackEverything breaks the usual trade-off between tracking few points for a long time or all points briefly, by representing video as persistent 3D scene tracks.
stories.more: Existing point-tracking models typically must choose between tracking a sparse set of query points over long time horizons or tracking all points across only short clips. TrackEverything represents videos as persistent 3D scene tracks in world coordinates, building on the insight that video is a 2D projection of an underlying 3D world. By de-duplicating these 3D scene representations, it decouples model complexity from video duration, letting it scale to longer footage.

items.title: TrackEverything: Long Horizon Dense Tracking via De-Duplicating 3D Scene Representations

We introduce TrackEverything, a 3D point tracker that breaks this trade-off by representing videos as persistent 3D scene tracks in world coordinates. stories.title: SLCA-GRPO fixes credit misattribution in tool-calling reinforcement learning
stories.summary: SLCA-GRPO addresses a failure mode in reinforcement learning for tool-calling agents, where gradient noise from natural-language summaries leaks into tool-decision tokens.
stories.more: Tool-calling agents produce heterogeneous outputs that interleave structured tool invocations with user-facing natural-language summaries, which creates a problem for standard on-policy RL algorithms like GRPO: they broadcast one trajectory-level reward to all tokens indiscriminately. This lets gradient noise from summary generation leak into tool-decision tokens, causing cross-segment credit misattribution and brittle training. SLCA-GRPO is proposed to resolve this misattribution.

stories.title: SAGE uses topological guidance to curb long-horizon reasoning biases
stories.summary: SAGE targets two biases that make long-horizon LLM reasoning brittle under sparse rewards: drifting toward locally plausible but unstable branches, and compounding small deviations.
stories.more: Long-horizon reasoning is a central challenge for large language models under sparse-reward conditions. The authors attribute this brittleness to two biases: an exploration bias that draws models toward locally plausible but structurally unstable reasoning branches, and a compounding bias where small local deviations accumulate across depth and suppress rare correct rewards. They introduce Symbolic Closure Analysis as a theoretical lens for characterizing these biases, underlying the SAGE method.

We argue that this brittleness arises from two biases induced by complex reasoning spaces: an exploration bias, where models are drawn toward locally plausible but structurally unstable branches, and a compounding bias, where small local deviations accumulate across depth and suppress rare rewards. stories.title: AgentWorld benchmarks long-horizon collaboration among multi-agent LLMs
stories.summary: AgentWorld is a new benchmark of 100 human-annotated tasks testing whether groups of 3 to 20 LLM agents can collaborate over 50+ steps in an MMORPG-style sandbox.
stories.more: Existing multi-agent benchmarks mostly test competitive settings, short interactions under 20 steps, or simply aggregate individual agent performance, which fails to isolate genuine collaboration ability. AgentWorld introduces 100 human-annotated tasks, plus 100 augmented variants, spanning 50-plus interaction rounds in a rich MMORPG sandbox. Tasks require 3 to 20 agents with asymmetric roles to collaborate over long horizons.

We introduce AgentWorld, a benchmark of 100 human-annotated tasks (with 100 augmented variants) for evaluating long-horizon, multi-agent collaboration. stories.title: IndicBankBench tests AI banking assistants for Indian retail banking
stories.summary: IndicBankBench is a 799-case benchmark evaluating whether language-model banking assistants handle Indian retail-banking tasks safely, beyond just checking their final answers.
stories.more: Banking assistants must use account-specific information to answer requests and often take actions through tools, but evaluating only the final response can miss serious errors, such as asking for information already provided, relying on stale context, picking the wrong account, or writing an invalid value after stating the correct one. IndicBankBench introduces 799 cases across five operational domains plus a capability/refusal domain, with twenty primary evaluation dimensions, for Indian retail banking.

stories.title: CARD personalizes text generation via cluster-level LoRA adapters
stories.summary: CARD clusters users by writing style and learns group-specific LoRA adapters, then adds reward-guided decoding for individual differences, to personalize text generation at scale.
stories.more: Adapting large language models to individual users is difficult because fine-grained personalization is in tension with scalable deployment. CARD is a hierarchical framework that first clusters users by shared stylistic patterns and learns group-specific LoRA adapters, enabling generalization and strong low-resource performance. It then adds reward-guided decoding to capture individual differences within each cluster.

items.title: CARD: Cluster-level Adaptation with Reward-guided Decoding for Personalized Text Generation
items.excerpt: Adapting large language models to individual users remains challenging due to the tension between fine-grained personalization and scalable deployment. We present CARD, a hierarchical framework that achieves effective personalization through progressive refinement. CARD first clusters users according to shared stylistic patterns and learns group-specific LoRA adapters, enabling robust generalization and strong low-resource performance. stories.title: Startup Basis says GPT-6 Astra halves tax-workbook completion time
stories.summary: Fintech startup Basis says OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra completed a 50-tab tax workbook twice as fast as the prior GPT-5.6 Sol model, citing stronger intent understanding.
stories.more: According to OpenAI's case study, Basis used GPT-6 Astra to complete a 50-tab tax workbook in half the time it previously took with GPT-5.6 Sol. Basis attributes part of the improvement to Astra's stronger understanding of user intent, which it says gives the company more confidence deploying the model in real-world tax work. The item is a customer case study published by OpenAI rather than an independent benchmark.

stories.title: Deepfake scam of her grandfather led this founder to build DetectifAI

stories.more: DetectifAI, a San Francisco startup, builds AI models small enough to run directly on smartphones to detect deepfake voices as they happen. The company is one of the contenders competing in the Startup Battlefield at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026. Its founder started the company after a voice deepfake impersonating a family member was used to scam her grandfather.

stories.title: Simon Willison notes S3 storage prices haven't dropped in a decade
stories.summary: Commenting on a Hacker News discussion, Simon Willison points out that AWS S3 storage pricing has been frozen at $0.023 per GB-month for a full decade after years of periodic cuts.
stories.more: Willison lists S3's historical price-per-GB-month drops, from $0.150 in 2006 down to $0.023 by December 2016, noting there has been no further reduction since then. He frames this as notable given S3's earlier pattern of periodic price cuts.

items.title: S3 Is the Future, S3 Is the Past
items.excerpt: My comment on S3 Is the Future, S3 Is the Past — Hacker News. One thing I find notable about S3 today is that, while it used to drop in price reasonably often, there hasn't been a price drop in a full decade : 2006-03-14 $0.150/GB-month 2010-11-01 $0.140/GB-month 2012-02-01 $0.125/GB-month 2012-12-01 $0.095/GB-month 2014-02-01 $0.085/GB-month 2014-04-01 $0.030/GB-month 2016-12-01 $0.023/GB-month Today it's still $0.023/GB-month.
